title: Flood Warning
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected. * WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday Nov 30. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 110 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the warned area. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .Heavy rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood Stage. The river may approach its record flood. For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Deland. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 5.7 feet. - Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 5.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising through Major Flood Stage, reaching 6.2 feet late this weekend. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 4.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels are forecast to hold near a crest of 13.1 feet through mid week before beginning a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week and into this weekend. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 13.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 13.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is forecast to remain steady near 13.1 feet through Thursday before gradually falling late this week into the weekend, remaining within Major Flood Stage. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: * WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides. * WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait, and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County. * WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots, roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 121 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding. - The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the average lowest daily tide. * Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue 11/24, +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.2 ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27. * West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM Tue 11/24, +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.1 ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27. * Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24, +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26, +7.4 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27 and +7.0 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28. - These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the San Francisco Bay and Delta. - Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at: * Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre dictions.html?id=9415144 * West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide predictions.html?id=9416131 * Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

title: Special Marine Warning
description: SMWMFL The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a * Special Marine Warning for... Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas... * Until 700 AM EST. * At 559 AM EST, severe thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from 49 nm southeast of Spiegel Grove to 25 nm east of Floyd's Wall Northeast, moving north at 20 knots. HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater. SOURCE...Radar. IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and suddenly higher waves. * Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.

title: Flood Advisory
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected. * WHERE...Northeastern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida... * WHEN...Until 745 AM EST. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 537 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms.
